nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 3$ be a natural number, let $F_n(k)$ be the $n$-fold iterated factorial of $k$, viewed as a real number, and for a real number $c$ and $m \ge 0$ let $E_m(10, c)$ be the $m$-fold iterate of $x \mapsto 10^x$ starting at $c$. nodes.title: Iterated factorials as base-$10$ power towers

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 3$ be a natural number and $F_n(k)$ the $n$-fold iterated factorial of $k$; for a real number $\beta$ let $\beta \uparrow\uparrow n$ be the $n$-fold iterate of $x \mapsto \beta^x$ starting at $1$. Then there is a sequence $(b_n)$ of real numbers such that $b_n > e^{1/e}$ and $F_n(k) = b_n \uparrow\uparrow n$ for every $n \ge 1$, and $(b_n)$ converges to a limit $b \le k!$.
nodes.title: Iterated factorials as tetrations

nodes.title: Iterated Gamma values as power towers

nodes.summary: Let $z > 1$ be a real number with $\Gamma(z) = z$, and let $b > z$. Let $b \uparrow\uparrow n$ be the $n$-fold iterate of $y \mapsto b^y$ starting at $1$, and $\Gamma^n$ the $n$-fold iterate of $\Gamma$. Then there is a convergent sequence $(x_n)$ of real numbers, strictly decreasing from some index on, such that $b \uparrow\uparrow n = \Gamma^n(x_n)$ for every $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Tetrations as iterated Gamma values

nodes.summary: Let $a, b > e^{1/e}$ be real numbers with $a \ne b$. For a real number $c$ and $m \ge 0$ let $E_m(b, c)$ be the $m$-fold iterate of $x \mapsto b^x$ starting at $c$ (the tower $b^{b^{\cdots^{c}}}$ with $m$ copies of $b$), and let $a \uparrow\uparrow n$ be the $n$-fold iterate of $x \mapsto a^x$ starting at $1$. nodes.title: Normalization of power towers

nodes.summary: Let $a, b > e^{1/e}$ be real numbers and $n > 0$ a natural number. Let $a \uparrow\uparrow n$ be the $n$-fold iterate of $x \mapsto a^x$ starting at $1$, and $E_p(b, c)$ the $p$-fold iterate of $x \mapsto b^x$ starting at $c$. Then there are a natural number $p$ and a real number $c$ with $1 < c \le b$ such that $a \uparrow\uparrow n = E_p(b, c)$.
nodes.title: Power towers rewritten in another base

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $j$ and $m$ let $F_j(m)$ be the $j$-fold iterated factorial $m!\cdots!$ (with $j$ factorials). Let $n, n' \ge 3$ and $k > k'$ be natural numbers. If $n' < F_{k-k'}(n)$, then $F_{k'}(n') < F_k(n)$.
nodes.title: Comparison of iterated factorials

nodes.summary: Let $a, b$ be real numbers with $e^{1/e} < a < b$. For $n \ge 0$ let $b \uparrow\uparrow n$ be the $n$-fold iterate of $x \mapsto b^x$ starting at $1$ (so $b \uparrow\uparrow 0 = 1$ and $b \uparrow\uparrow 1 = b$), and let $a_n = \log_a^{(n)}(b \uparrow\uparrow n)$ be its $n$-fold iterated base-$a$ logarithm, so that $a_0 = 1$. Then the sequence $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ is strictly increasing and converges to a real number.
nodes.title: Iterated logarithms of power towers increase to a limit

nodes.summary: Let $b \ge e$ and, for $m \ge 0$, let $E_m(b, b)$ be the $m$-fold iterate of $x \mapsto b^x$ started at $b$, so that $E_0(b, b) = b$ and $E_{m+1}(b, b) = b^{E_m(b, b)}$. Then for every integer $n > 0$, $E_{n+1}(b, b) < \Gamma(E_n(b, b))$.
nodes.title: Gamma of an iterated exponential exceeds the next iterate

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
